name: The Passion Week, Crucifixion, and Resurrection
path: New Testament Studies: Life and Doctrine in Christ
The Gospels and the Life of Christ

objectives.text: Retell how the crowds welcomed Jesus into Jerusalem by waving branches and shouting Hosanna
Recall that Jesus died on the cross, was buried, and rose again on the third day, leaving the tomb empty
Describe how Jesus washed his disciples' feet and explain the example of service he told them to follow
Summarize the Last Supper and explain what Jesus said the bread and the cup represent
Describe Jesus' prayer in the Garden of Gethsemane and what it shows about his submission to the Father's will
Explain the Reformed teaching that Jesus died as a substitute, bearing the punishment for the sins of his people
Identify people to whom the risen Jesus appeared, including Mary Magdalene, the travelers to Emmaus, and Thomas
Compare Judas' betrayal and Peter's denial, including how each story ends
Construct a timeline of the major events of Passion Week from the triumphal entry to the resurrection
Identify Jesus' predictions of his death and resurrection and describe how the disciples responded to them
Explain how Jesus' clearing of the temple during Passion Week intensified the religious leaders' opposition to him
Explain how events of the Passion fulfill Old Testament prophecies
Analyze the Jewish and Roman trials of Jesus, including the charges brought and the roles of Caiaphas, Pilate, and Herod
Analyze the seven sayings of Jesus from the cross in light of their Gospel context and Old Testament background
Compare the Passover in Exodus with the Last Supper and the crucifixion to explain why Scripture calls Christ our Passover lamb
Explain the meaning of the darkness and the tearing of the temple curtain at Jesus' death
Explain the significance of the resurrection for justification and for the future resurrection of believers
Distinguish Christ's state of humiliation from his state of exaltation as the Westminster Standards describe them
Explain how the Reformed tradition interprets the Apostles' Creed phrases about Christ's burial and descent into hell
Compare the four Gospel accounts of the crucifixion and identify the distinct emphasis of each evangelist
Analyze the Gospel accounts and Roman crucifixion practice as evidence that Jesus truly died
Evaluate the historical evidence for the resurrection against alternative explanations such as theft, swoon, and hallucination
Evaluate major theories of the atonement against Scripture, explaining why the Reformed tradition holds penal substitution as central
Explain the Reformed doctrine of definite atonement and the passages its defenders cite
Create a written or oral synthesis explaining how the cross and the empty tomb together accomplish redemption and union with Christ

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies: triumphal entry, cross and empty tomb, foot washing, Last Supper, Gethsemane, substitutionary death, Judas and Peter, trials, seven sayings, Passover, resurrection significance, timeline, and the final synthesis. Merged the separate K to 2 recall items into fuller statements and replaced 'Observe' and 'Name' with observable verbs. Moved the timeline down to grade 5. Recast the medical aspects item as analyzing evidence that Jesus truly died, and recast 'defend as historical fact' as evaluating evidence against alternative theories. Added Jesus' passion predictions, the temple clearing, prophecy fulfillment, signs at his death, resurrection appearances, humiliation and exaltation, burial and descent in the Creed, comparison of the four Gospel accounts, atonement theories, and definite atonement. Added scripture and confession anchors where each objective rests on them.
